title: fix(rest,metadata-protocol): a public form's intake withdrawal at any metadata layer holds; layering can only narrow intake
body:
Fixes #21835

Clause-②: yes (widening)

Fixes a regression introduced after 17.6.0 (with #21420); it should land before 17.7.0 is cut.

## What

Per the rulings recorded on #21835: a public form's withdrawal is a kill switch, layering can only narrow anonymous intake, a withdrawal closes the **same form** only, and only an **explicit** withdrawal counts.

- **Anonymous doors (`GET /forms/:slug`, `POST /forms/:slug/submit`).** Both use one resolver. When an organization is resolved, the env-wide view layer beneath it is read as well, and a form is served only when no layer explicitly withdraws **that same form** — the same view (by name) at the same slot (nested form, the same `formViews` key, or the flattened config). Other views that share the public slug never close each other.
- **What counts as a withdrawal.** A layer's body of the same view, at the same slot, names the same slug in `publicLink` and does not open it (`enabled` or `allowAnonymous` not true). Not a withdrawal: a sharing with no link (raw, or schema-parsed with its `false` defaults), a cleared or changed link, a removed sharing block, or no body of the view at that layer. The public data collection docs page gains a "Withdraw a public form" section with these rules.
- **Write door.** An org-scoped `view` save in the organization the doors read is refused with `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` when it would leave open a form the env-wide layer explicitly withdraws — judged by the doors' own predicate, so re-saving an overlay that was already open before the withdrawal is refused too. Container-shaped bodies are expanded the way the list read serves them before judging. The message names both remedies.
- **Intentional reversal.** The earlier behaviour in which an organization overlay re-published a form the package had withdrawn is reversed. A form with no env-wide word on it stays organization-publishable (#21420), and the #21473 anchors and #21566 field allowlist are unchanged.
- **Public surface:** `@objectstack/metadata-core` adds one export, `anonymousFormIntakeWithdrawnIn` (`minor`). `@objectstack/rest` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` are `patch`.
- **Not gated at write time:** metadata rollback and commit revert (the doors still keep such a form closed at read time); noted in the changeset.

## Tests

Measured at `e8778acb96`:

- `@objectstack/metadata-core`: 18 files, 394 passed.
- `@objectstack/rest`: 260 files, 4906 passed, 326 skipped.
- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: 214 files (3 skipped), 27752 passed, 19 skipped.
- Typecheck green for all three and dogfood.
- Dogfood (real showcase boot): the layered-withdrawal suite 5/5 (including the re-save refusal) and the five sibling public-form suites 20/20.
- Coverage: two views sharing a slug do not close each other (one read, with and without an organization, and across layers); a cleared link is not a withdrawal; a parsed link-less sharing is not a withdrawal; re-saving an already-open overlay is refused; a container-shaped save is judged after expansion.
- Ablation (source set back to the base blobs, packages rebuilt): 3 / 4 / 4 tests red across metadata-core / rest / metadata-protocol; restored to HEAD.
- Gates: 92 of 95 derived run green; `check:skill-examples`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:type-check-debt` are NOT MEASURED locally (workspace-wide prerequisites) and left to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- Gating rollback / revert at write time is a possible follow-up (it needs the restored body before the repository writes it); read-time enforcement already holds.
- Two installed apps publishing the same slug is a separate concern (slug collision), out of scope here.
